chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sukkari narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Zakariya al-Jawhari, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Umara, from his father, from al-Sadiq, Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father, Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father, al-Husayn ibn Ali, from his father, Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them all)

He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) said: Indeed, I am leaving among you the Two Weighty Things: the Book of Allah, and my Family, my Household. And indeed, they will never be separated until they come to me at the Basin like these two – and he joined his two index fingers together. Then Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari stood up to him and said: O Messenger of Allah, and who is your Family? He said: Ali, al-Hasan, al-Husayn, and the Imams from the descendants of al-Husayn until the Day of Resurrection.

key_terms.الثَّقَلَيْنِ: The Two Weighty Things (Quran and Ahl al-Bayt)
key_terms.الْحَوْضَ: The Basin (of the Prophet on Judgment Day)

ai.seo_question: Who are the Ahl al-Bayt mentioned in the Hadith of Al-Thaqalayn?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, this narration reinforces the Shia doctrine of *Al-Thaqalayn* by explicitly defining the 'Ahl al-Bayt' not merely as the Prophet's household, but specifically as Ali, Hasan, Husayn, and the twelve Imams descending from Husayn. The hadith emphasizes their inseparability from the Quran until they meet at the Pool of Kawthar, establishing a theological framework where the Imams serve as the living, authoritative interpretation of Divine Revelation. This specific chain of transmission (*isnad*) highlights the continuity of authority from the Prophet through the Ahl al-Bayt, a cornerstone of Shia exegesis and jurisprudence.
